objective: Register a three-path, owner-operated local encrypted credential rekey utility; code preparation and synthetic qualification only.
requirements: Owner approved safe local recovery preparation at 08:12 UTC on 7 October 2026; parent dispatch explicitly authorizes finite registration before product edits, reviewed synthetic-only implementation and hidden-prompt handoff. Jira APBRA-160 PLAN 10605 records this direct authority. The existing Confluence 03.08 v3 source is historical context for protected credential references, not a claim it accepted this new recovery utility.

Preserve every credential reference ID, company/profile associated-data binding, created metadata, revocation state and immutable Tenant Settings/history. Re-encrypt existing rows in place using authenticated AES-GCM, fresh nonces and a distinct active key version; authenticate old and replacement ciphertext before one atomic commit. Include revoked and historically referenced rows; never replace the provider credential or settings references.

Owner personally generates and enters replacements locally through hidden TTY prompts. No secrets in arguments, echo, logs, exceptions, plaintext files, public evidence or chat. Fail closed without TTY, malformed keyrings, absent historical keys, wrong target confirmation, missing backup/maintenance acknowledgement, database/protocol failures or failed authentication. Bounded fixed error messages only.

Utility is a maintenance operation with PostgreSQL transaction/locking, preview-only explicit target confirmation, dry-run default and a separate explicit commit confirmation. No provider/network/cloud operation other than the explicitly selected local database. Require local-loopback PostgreSQL target and restrict to development/test profile. Do not implicitly use environment bootstrap or seed credentials.

Agents implement and test only synthetic keys, credentials and isolated disposable data. Do not read/decrypt/re-encrypt real provider credentials, generate or submit live replacements, execute on real data, edit preview/security settings, remove old keys, rotate provider credentials, delete evidence, install preview changes or make paid calls. Local user execution requires separate coordinated handoff and explicit authorization.

Keep old-key recovery for existing encrypted database backups. Successful current-row rekeying does not sanitize retained backups or private tool-output retention and does not prove production security. Saved report request, CSV, evidence, history and protected artifacts remain untouched.
adrs: Separate registration, implementation, independent exact-head review, hosted CI and authorized manual merges. Registration itself changes governance only. This task does not broaden existing editable-draft 26 paths.

No bulk rekey facility currently exists. Add narrow store support and an owner-operated CLI; preserve identity/AAD and perform atomic authenticated migration rather than provider-secret replacement. No schema or dependency changes.
